artifacts.summary: Confirms validate-return-meta.sh has zero partial_progress coverage and zero executing call sites; pins the integration point to orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (orchestrator-postflight.sh is orphaned); surfaces a critical noise hazard (status-vocabulary false positives for non-canonical-vocabulary agents) not named in the dispatch and specifies the partial_progress-output-gated call-site design that avoids it; proposes a new RETURN_META_SCHEMA_VIOLATION Signal A defect class.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrator-postflight.sh is an orphaned script with no live callers (confirmed by its own header, skill-git-workflow/SKILL.md's 'Relationship to orchestrator-postflight.sh' section, and skill-base.sh:909's comment). The only live per-task postflight body for both /orchestrate engines is scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, invoked from skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md. When a task asks 'where should a new postflight check be wired', orchestrator-postflight.sh is never the answer despite its name and Stage-numbered header comments suggesting otherwise.

lint-agent-contracts.sh:619-635 records a deliberately-deferred blocker: wiring validate-return-meta.sh's strict status-vocabulary check (Check 2) into any live chokepoint would break registered agents with intentional non-canonical success vocabularies (legal-analysis-agent's 'consulted', slidev-assembly-agent's 'assembled', every filetypes/* vocabulary) until orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh's 3-value success-acceptance set is widened (a separate, blocked item). Any new call site for validate-return-meta.sh's full exit code -- even a warn-only one -- risks resurrecting this as false-positive noise against correctly-behaving agents; gate on the specific check's output instead of the aggregate exit code when only one check's violation is the target.
